span.p:
LEGEND
Blue = bounded LLM reasoning
Purple = LangGraph runtime/state
Green = deterministic code
Red = security or human authority
Cyan = verified output
Yellow = decision plus rejected alternative

div.style: color: rgb(69, 26, 3) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
DECISION D1 · Keep React only as the presentation layer
Reason: rich streaming and approval UX are useful.
Rejected: putting orchestration in React because browser refreshes,
multiple tabs, and client cancellation cannot own durable execution.

div.style: color: rgb(69, 26, 3) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
DECISION D2 · Single-user identity now, identity-ready state schema
Reason: harden the core before introducing tenant and row-level policy.
Rejected now: multi-user RBAC because it multiplies test combinations
without improving the current agent workflow.

div.style: color: rgb(69, 26, 3) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
DECISION D3 · LangGraph owns orchestration; LangChain supplies model/tool adapters
Reason: durable state, explicit transitions, interrupts, bounded loops, and replay.
Rejected: the current global while-true ReAct loop because stopping,
recovery, and provider behavior are model-dependent.

div.style: color: rgb(69, 26, 3) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
DECISION D4 · Checkpoint after side effects, not after every token
Reason: resume safely without duplicating queries, reports, or publications.
Rejected: memory-only state because a process crash loses approvals and progress.
Rejected now: Temporal because its operational cost is excessive for one user.

div.style: color: rgb(69, 26, 3) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
DECISION D5 · One graph with two specialists, not three peer agents
Reason: extraction and execution are security-sensitive deterministic services.
Analyst reasons; Builder authors; Reviewer is optional and read-only.
Rejected: Extractor/Executor/Validator peer agents because handoffs duplicate state,
increase cost, blur authority, and allow one LLM to approve another LLM.

div.style: color: rgb(69, 26, 3) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
DECISION D6 · ReAct exists only inside bounded Analyst/Builder nodes
Reason: ambiguity, SQL repair, and visual selection need judgment.
Rejected: ReAct for credentials, querying, validation, versioning, or publication
because those operations have known deterministic transitions.

div.style: color: rgb(69, 26, 3) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
DECISION D7 · Provider-neutral interface, provider-specific packages
Reason: consistent graph state while preserving native model capabilities.
Rejected: three copied provider loops because fixes and policies drift over time.

div.style: color: rgb(69, 26, 3) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
DECISION D8 · Keep MCP as the tool protocol
Reason: dynamic discovery isolates the agent from Microsoft and custom tool changes.
Rejected: direct SDK calls inside reasoning nodes because they couple orchestration,
credentials, schemas, and vendor-specific transport.

div.style: color: rgb(69, 26, 3) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
DECISION D9 · Approval belongs to a durable interrupt
Reason: a suspended run must survive disconnect or backend restart.
Rejected: a blocking browser callback because it loses state and cannot be audited.

div.style: color: rgb(69, 26, 3) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
DECISION D10 · BigQuery access is a service, never an extraction agent
Reason: least privilege and reproducible enforcement must not depend on prompts.
Rejected: giving an LLM the Google client because it could bypass allowlists,
cost ceilings, audit fields, and stable error handling.

div.style: color: rgb(69, 26, 3) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
DECISION D11 · Validate both explicit SQL resources and dry-run resolved tables
Reason: text checks catch obvious escapes; BigQuery resolves aliases, views, and syntax.
Rejected: regex-only validation because SQL resolution is not reliably lexical.
Rejected: IAM-only protection because application policy may be narrower than IAM.

div.style: color: rgb(69, 26, 3) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
DECISION D12 · Generate a real semantic-model connection definition
Reason: a catalog alone cannot make Desktop query BigQuery.
Rejected: embedding Google credentials because PBIP is source-controlled,
portable, and not an acceptable secret store.

div.style: color: rgb(69, 26, 3) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
DECISION D13 · DirectQuery is default; Import is an explicit option
Reason: local-first analysis should see current data without copying datasets.
Tradeoff: DirectQuery depends on connectivity and source performance;
use Import when interactivity/offline operation outweighs freshness.

div.style: color: rgb(69, 26, 3) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
DECISION D14 · LLM produces DashboardSpec, never PBIR JSON directly
Reason: a narrow typed contract enables deterministic compilation and validation.
Rejected: free-form PBIR generation because schema drift and hallucinated fields
would enter source artifacts before validation.

div.style: color: rgb(69, 26, 3) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
DECISION D15 · Immutable revisions plus optimistic concurrency
Reason: every mutation is auditable and rollback is reliable.
Rejected: editing the active report in place because partial failure destroys
the last known-good version.

div.style: color: rgb(69, 26, 3) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
DECISION D16 · Deterministic QA has final authority
Reason: security, schema, and semantic correctness require reproducible rules.
Rejected: an LLM validator as final approver because confident agreement
between agents is not evidence of correctness.

div.style: color: rgb(69, 26, 3) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
DECISION D17 · Local-first core; Fabric is an optional output plane
Reason: analysis and authoring remain usable without tenant admin privileges.
Rejected: Fabric-first execution because Entra/Fabric access would block
local development, qualification, and single-user iteration.

div.style: color: rgb(69, 26, 3) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
DECISION D18 · Idempotent cloud workflow, not a cloud execution agent
Reason: API mutations and long-running operations need exact IDs and terminal states.
Rejected: letting an agent improvise retries because it can duplicate resources
or report success before Fabric completes the operation.

div.style: color: rgb(69, 26, 3) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
DECISION D19 · Retry by typed failure class
Reason: throttling may recover; security and deterministic validation will not.
Rejected: generic automatic retry because it wastes cost and can repeat mutations.

div.style: color: rgb(69, 26, 3) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
DECISION D20 · Observability is replaceable; audit evidence is mandatory
Reason: enterprise review needs stable local records independent of a SaaS vendor.
Rejected: making LangSmith mandatory because privacy, cost, or connectivity
must not prevent local execution.
